ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $l_{1} \parallel l_{2}$, $l_{2} \parallel l_{3}$, line $a$ and $b$ intersect $l_{1}$, $l_{2}$, $l_{3}$ at points A, B, C and points D, E, F respectively. If $AB = 3$, $DE = 2$, $BC = 6$, what is the value of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $l_{1} \parallel l_{2} \parallel l_{3}$,\\
it follows that $\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{DE}{EF}$,\\
thus $\frac{3}{6}=\frac{2}{EF}$\\
Solving yields: EF=\boxed{4}

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three parallel straight lines arranged from top to bottom, labeled l1, l2, l3. The oblique line a intersects these three parallel lines in order at A, B, C, and another approximately vertical straight line b intersects these three parallel lines in order at D, E, F. Therefore AB and BC are two adjacent segments on the same transversal a, and DE and EF are the corresponding two adjacent segments on another transversal b. Reasoning: Because l1 ∥ l2 ∥ l3, according to the theorem that parallel lines divide line segments proportionally, there is AB/BC = DE/EF. Substituting AB=3, BC=6, DE=2, gives 3/6 = 2/EF. Cross-multiplying gives 3EF = 12, so EF = 4.

From the image, note that transversals a and b are not parallel and would meet if extended above the top line; call their intersection P.
